Subject: Post-demo: model fit + quantization trade study (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) - next steps

Hi Joe / Ellie —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end based on the demo and your goals (throughput for batch scoring + inline latency for agents):

What we recommended on the call:
- Candidate models: Llama 3 70B (baseline), Llama 3 13B (cost-sensitive), and an instruction-tuned open LLM you mentioned for retrieval-augmented generation.
- Quantization profiles to evaluate: AWQ (8-bit optimized), GPTQ (4/8-bit variants), and an FP8 profile for hardware-accelerated throughput tests.
- Tradeoffs to watch: AWQ typically preserves quality with good throughput improvements for generation-heavy workloads; GPTQ can push to smaller memory footprints but sometimes shows narrow regression for specific prompt families; FP8 gives best peak throughput on supported HW but requires careful overflow/scale tuning.

Attachments I dropped into the Drive link below:
- acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (your initial prompt set we discussed)
- redwood_quant_trade_study_template.xlsx (suggested test matrix + metrics)

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a holdout prompt/eval set (we can use the attached acme_prompt_set_v1 as a starting point).
2) We run a 2-week trade study comparing AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 on the 70B and 13B models (we'll report: token-level latency p50/p95, throughput, token cost, and per-prompt quality diffs using your eval metrics).
3) Lukas (SE) will pair with your infra folks for runtime config and any KMS/network questions.
4) If results look good, we scope a 30-day pilot on Dedicated with a controlled rollback path.

Can you confirm internal owners for the eval set and an expected timeline for share? If you prefer, we can set up the initial trade study week starting Nov 16.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit + quantization trade study (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) - next steps

Great questions — answers inline below and a proposed pricing ballpark.

1) GPTQ regressions: short answer — rare but observable on narrow instruction templates that heavily rely on subtle tokenization/context behaviors (e.g., multi-step summarization prompts where hallucination sensitivity increases). We saw in a recent Redwood trade study (linked) a 2–4% drop in exact-match or BLEU-like metrics on specific prompt subsets for GPTQ-4-bit on 70B vs float baseline; AWQ maintained quality within 0.5–1% on the same slices. We'll include per-prompt diffs in the report so you can make an informed call.

2) FP8 safety checks: Redwood's FP8 pipeline includes dynamic range scans, per-layer scaling heuristics, and a validation sweep that compares a sample of inference outputs vs baseline to flag skewed distributions. We do recommend extra gating in production: A/B canary and automated regression thresholds tied to your evaluation metrics. Lukas can share the specific validation scripts.

3) Cost estimate (2-week trade study):
- Test cluster (4x A100s equivalent) reserved for 10 working days: approx $12k–$18k (variation depends on simultaneous vs batch runs).
- Engineering support (SE time + report): ~ 3–4 days of SE effort (included in initial eval credit; additional days billed per SOW).

Next steps:
- We'll start provisional runs on Nov 16 — please confirm by Nov 12 that you can share the 1k prompts.
- Lukas/Neha: can you confirm availability for a 30–45 minute kickoff next week to align on metrics and infra?

Thanks —
Marissa
